messages:
Maria: quick nsys + perfetto run on the canary with the new size-based early-flush batching heuristic (dedicated pool). tl;dr: attn_fwd jumped to ~42% GPU time, kv_concat and memcpy also up. posting top kernels + occupancy suspects — need help triaging.

Maria: ```
nsys profile -o /tmp/canary_run --trace=cuda,osrt ./serve_canary.sh --model rwd-13b --batch 32
```
TOP (nsys) by GPU time:
1) attn_fwd — 42.1%
2) matmul_1 — 12.4%
3) kv_concat — 9.8%
4) softmax — 6.7%
5) memcpy_h2d — 5.9%
occupancy (sample): attn_fwd SM% 56, matmul_1 SM% 78, kv_concat SM% 32

Ajay: is this the kernel-variant selector kicking in? did the compiler pick a different matmul/attn kernel because of changed sequence length distribution?

Maria: yes — compile log shows kernel_variant="mix_fp16_tiled_v2" for attn_fwd on this run. previous stable runs used mix_fp16_tiled_v1. suspect the variant cost model changed behavior at larger merged prefixes.

Jen: kv_concat rising makes sense — early-flush merges more prefixes into single batch => bigger KV buffers and extra memcpy/concat work. can we get L2 / dram breakdown?

Simon: nvprof quick-summary: attn_fwd shows ~38% memory pipe stalls, L2 hit-rate down ~12% vs baseline. nvlink queue depth higher too (more H2D chatter).

perf-bot: Trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/p/trace-1912345678 (nsys+perfetto). auto-summarizer: recommends checking kernel tiling choice and L2-aware prefetch heuristics.

Ajay: quick experiment idea: cap prefix-merge in the heuristic to 8 (instead of unlimited), run 100 synthetic requests and compare top kernel pct. i can run A/B if someone thumbs up.

Maria: please run A/B. if attn_fwd drops back to ~18-20% when cap=8 we either pin the heuristic or add a KV-size-aware fallback in the router.

Jen: also try forcing kernel variant: export FORCE_KERNEL=fp16_tiled_v1 and re-run — will tell if variant alone triggers the regression vs the merged-batch size.

Simon: i'll schedule a perf job to capture nvprof metrics: nvprof --metrics l2_hit_rate,dram_read_throughput -- ./serve_canary.sh ... put results in perf queue.

Maria: :thumbsup: thanks. collecting results from Ajay + Simon, will open canary rollback PR if A/B indicates clear perf regression.
